answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Cider press record with orchard trust attestation flips the bet — each record is pressings logged by the orchard trust, so a hundred fakes need a hundred real orchards — and the willow lands on the attacker instead. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the pulse of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The delta is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
